gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns an unjustified identification of the closed residual target with the closure of strict sublevels and the resulting fixed-threshold bounds. ISSUE-002 instead concerns omission of nonsingularity from the analytic witness relation; it does not recognize the target-set mismatch or boundary-point approximation obligation.

The gold issue is failure of strict threshold membership decisions to stabilize despite numerical convergence, invalidating the claimed finite-set limit. ISSUE-003 concerns applying a block spectral lemma to a zero-measure block and does not diagnose oscillation at a threshold or the missing stabilization argument.

The gold issue is a null direction in a finite-dimensional dictionary when the measure lacks full support, causing failure of L1-to-uniform compactness and unbounded quadrature error. ISSUE-003 instead identifies a zero-measure singleton used outside a positive-measure block-decomposition hypothesis; it does not recognize the null-direction or quadrature defect.

Both identify the impossibility of the claimed Polish code space with a Borel evaluation map representing every Borel function. Consequently the witness relation is not established as Borel and the projection argument does not establish analyticity.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The universal Borel evaluator/code-space premise used to make the witness relation Borel is false, so the claimed analyticity of A_{z_0} is unsupported.

component_coverage.gold_component: The purported universal Polish coding of all Borel functions with a Borel evaluation map is impossible, invalidating the projection-based analyticity argument.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly states that no such standard Borel parameterization and Borel evaluation exist, and draws the same consequence for the Borel witness set and analytic projection.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue is that the greedy priority recursion destroys a Silver tree and therefore its claimed spectral equivalence and forward lemma are false. ISSUE-004 concerns the separate definitional failure when the recursion outputs bottom and the odometer is undefined; it does not diagnose the false greedy maximality or the resulting bounded-period counterexample.

Both identify that the recursion can output bottom even though the odometer is defined only on {0,1,*}^m, making the displayed update and hence F_S or Ψ(S) undefined on some trees. Both connect this to failure of the claimed total map and its dependent results.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The construction applies the odometer to a bottom-valued recursion output outside its domain, so the purported all-tree map is not defined.

component_coverage.gold_component: The failure branch yields u_m(S)=⊥ while the odometer is defined only for ternary words, so the constructed map is undefined for some trees.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 explicitly identifies the bottom output, the undefined F_S, and the contradiction with totality of Ψ on Tree_2.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue is failure of the general countable-block approximate-spectrum union equality because approximate vectors can escape through blocks with no uniformly attained lower bound. ISSUE-003 instead concerns a zero-measure singleton violating a positive-block-measure hypothesis; it does not recognize the varying-block residual construction or the missing uniform resolvent estimate.
